messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — High error rate and 95th latency spike for /v1/generate on prod (region us-east-1). Affected customers: two mid-market tenants. Trigger: kv-cache miss storm + batching backlog. Pager runbook: https://go/runbooks/inference-pager

sam: acked. I'm oncall. digging into kvcache metrics now.

anya: adding context — we just rolled quantized v2.1 yesterday in canary, but only saw small perf delta there. Could be traffic shape + batch size interaction.

sam: confirmed. Grafana: kvcache miss rate jumped x10 at 22:14 UTC, batch queue depth up to 180. latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 2.1s. attaching short logs:
```
2026-03-17T22:14:12Z runtime: kvcache miss id=abc123 shard=5
2026-03-17T22:14:12Z runtime: enqueue batch size=64 model=gpt-open-q2 quant=4bit
2026-03-17T22:14:13Z runtime: kernel fallback slow-path
```

miguel: temporary mitigation — can we switch affected routes to non-quantized variant and reduce max_batch_size?

jia: we have a compatible non-quant model (v2.0) in the catalog. I can trigger a policy-based fallback for those tenant routes.

sam: please do that, jia. Also lowering max_batch_size from 64->16 on those pods. Doing a canary rollout now.

jia: started fallback rollout to v2.0 for tenant-a and tenant-b routes. ETA ~2m.

ryan: FYI product team, customer-ops notified tenant-a support. tenant-b autopilot alerted their SRE. Notifying product-ops for any customer comms.

product-ops: thanks — tracking. Any measurable customer impact?

sam: preliminary: 30m window with 10% requests erroring (~5xx) and median latency doubled for affected tenant traffic during spike. No data exfiltration. Customers experienced tardy responses and a few failed requests.

anya: root cause hypothesis: quantized kernel path + sudden KV cache invalidation (likely due to TTL cascade from evictions) caused a high miss rate which combined with previously-tuned large batch sizes to overwhelm scheduler and cause kernel fallbacks.

miguel: remediation action list I propose: 1) ensure kv cache TTL smoothing + backpressure, 2) add circuit-breaker to disable large batches when miss_rate > threshold, 3) create a safe fallback policy for quantized models during miss storms, 4) audit the recent quant rollout for binary compatibility in fallback path.

sam: agreed. I'm creating a tracking ticket now. TICKET-4892: "kv-miss-burst -> batching overload -> quant fallback storm". Assigning owners.

sam: owners: kv cache + runtime: miguel; batching scheduler: anya; quant/model infra: jia; postmortem lead: sam.

jia: will open a model validation PR to add a runtime integration test that simulates miss storms against quantized kernels.

anya: I'll add a scheduler gating change to rate-limit batch growth when backend latencies exceed threshold.

miguel: will add TTL smoothing and tunable hysteresis for kvcache evictions.

product-ops: can we schedule a postmortem sync? Prefer tomorrow 11:00am PT.

sam: works for me. jia/anya/miguel?

jia: yes.

anya: yes.

miguel: yes.

sam: ok scheduled. Postmortem doc: https://go/pm/kvcache-batch-quant-4892 (I'll draft initial timeline + impact summary).

sam: immediate action items (owner — ETA):
- disable quantized variant as fallback policy for affected tenant routes (jia) — DONE (22:17 UTC)
- reduce max_batch_size on affected pods (sam) — DONE (22:19 UTC)
- create TICKET-4892 and initial postmortem doc (sam) — DONE (22:28 UTC)
- add monitoring alert for kv_cache_miss_rate sudden delta (miguel) — in progress
- add scheduler backpressure gating (anya) — in progress

product-ops: note for customer comms: tenant-a saw 14 failed requests flagged as "retryable" — we recommend outbound comms that issue was mitigated and that retries should succeed; offer follow-up if they see persistent errors.

sam: follow-up: we should add a low-latency fallback tier to avoid global batch spikes (design topic for next sprint).

jia: I'll include a regression test for quant kernels and a runbook addition to force fallback to non-quant if miss_rate > 5% for 1m.

anya: will prototype batch gating in a feature branch and link to the ticket.

miguel: adding notes to infra changelog and will coordinate a small perf test in staging that simulates TTL eviction waves.

sam: thanks team. final note before postmortem — no customer data loss, mitigations reverted to normal configs after 40m. Closing live pager.

incident-bot: Pager closed by sam at 22:55 UTC. Postmortem meeting scheduled 2026-03-18T18:00:00Z (11:00 PT).
